clue.text: Artist going to bank, once in a blue moon

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword artist
to bank on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: A painter heads to the riverbank only on very rare occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to' simply joins the two pieces; 'bank' is the verb (bank on), not a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening once in a blue moon happens only seldom, an idiom for great infrequency.

clue.text: Hotel guest and I study the others outside

indicators.note: the others are placed outside, so their word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: the rest means the others
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: A guest at a hotel goes off to work in a quiet room while everyone else waits outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel's lodger who is staying in the building is described as living there for the time being.

clue.text: Hospital doctor and nurse must take on board the main point, right?

indicators.note: taking something on board means holding it within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to nurse a child is to rear it
the gist is the main point of something

explanation.surface: A hospital doctor and a nurse must grasp the key idea, correct?
explanation.walkthrough: 'nurse' is a verb meaning bring up, not a hospital worker. In British hospitals a registrar is a senior grade of doctor below consultant.
explanation.definitionFit: In the UK a registrar is a mid-ranking hospital physician in training to become a consultant.

clue.text: Awfully loud game

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A board game played very noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a simple board game with counters raced home by dice throws.

clue.text: Clearly identified remedy

definitions.meaning: precise, clearly defined, as in a particular instance
a medicine targeted at one particular illness, an old medical noun

explanation.surface: A cure that has been precisely pinpointed.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means precise or particular; as an old medical noun it named a drug acting on a single disease.

clue.text: Girl, extremely posh, foolish to be set up

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters, first and last, of the next word
in a down clue, being set up means raised, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: silly means foolish

explanation.surface: A very upper-class young woman is foolishly framed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns SILLY into YLLIS, read upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Phyllis is a female forename, and girl's names are a common crossword definition.

clue.text: Force prisoner to prepare ground, breaking stones

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so one piece splits the other

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight unit, used for the plural as well
to train is to prepare, as for a race

explanation.surface: A convict is made to get the earth ready by smashing rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAIN sits inside ST. A stone is a British unit of weight (14 lb), abbreviated ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A constraint is a restriction or compulsion, the pressure that holds someone back.

clue.text: Overlook unfinished smithy

indicators.note: unfinished means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to overlook something is to forget it

explanation.surface: Disregard a blacksmith's workshop left half-built.
explanation.definitionFit: A forge is a blacksmith's workshop with its furnace, the same place as a smithy.

clue.text: Modest tea's prepared after church

indicators.note: after puts the church abbreviation first, the rest following it
tea is prepared by brewing, and here its letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A demure cup of tea is made once the church service ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and decent in behaviour, a near synonym of demure.

clue.text: First half of Cats penned by composer in secret

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the composer's name surrounds the other piece

parts.note: Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

indicators.note: taking the first half of a four-letter word gives its opening two letters

explanation.surface: Part of a musical about felines is kept under wraps by the songwriter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' puts the first two letters of Cats inside the composer's name. Cats is a well-known musical, so the surface invites a theatre reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcane means mysterious and understood only by a few, so known only to insiders.

clue.text: Cheese wise, ahead of race?

indicators.note: ahead of puts the first piece in front of the second

parts.note: a sage person is wise
the Derby is a famous horse race run at Epsom

explanation.surface: A clever cheese that arrives before the horse race starts.
explanation.walkthrough: Sage Derby is an English cheese marbled green with sage; the Derby is Britain's best-known flat horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage Derby is a type of English cheese flavoured with the herb.

clue.text: Almost typical operatic work

indicators.note: almost means the word stops just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: normal means typical

explanation.surface: A nearly standard piece of opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is the opera by Bellini about a druid priestess.

clue.text: Small amount of dead wood

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A little bit of lifeless timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash is a small quantity added, as a dash of milk.

clue.text: Canon circulated-odd letters from money market

indicators.note: circulated means sent round, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a canon is a law or rule

indicators.note: odd means strange, so these letters are put in a strange order

explanation.surface: A church canon circulated some peculiar letters from the financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulated' gives WAL from LAW; 'odd' rearranges LETTERS into LSTREET. 'odd letters' looks like alternate letters, but it is an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall Street in New York is the centre of US finance, its name standing for the stock market.

clue.text: Pity draper breaking Beatles record

indicators.note: breaking suggests smashing apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Feel sorry for the cloth merchant who beat a band's chart record.
explanation.definitionFit: Day Tripper is a 1965 single by the Beatles.

clue.text: Raced back to judge to tell the story

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: ran means raced
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: Someone hurried back to the referee to recount what happened.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to recount events in sequence, as a storyteller does.

clue.text: Song easily startled social worker inside

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: a shy animal is timid and easily alarmed
an ant is a social insect, a worker in a colony

explanation.surface: A nervous song with a care worker in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' means an insect living in a colony, not a council employee.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a sailors' work song, sung while hauling ropes.

clue.text: Taste before gathering in fruit

parts.note: a tang is a sharp taste

indicators.note: gathering means collecting up and holding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Sample the food before collecting fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' has the old word for before wrap round IN; 'in' looks like a link word but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small orange citrus fruit like a mandarin.

clue.text: Disown cure, none having been suitably treated

indicators.note: being treated means processed or worked on, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Reject a remedy when nobody has been properly cared for.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce is to give up or formally reject a claim or person, as in disowning.

clue.text: In favour of side dropping amateur, for the time being

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: dropping means leaving out a member, so one letter is removed

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: Backing a team that has just cut its non-professional player, but only temporarily.
explanation.walkthrough: TEAM drops A to give TEM. Pro tem is short for the Latin pro tempore.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro tem is a Latin phrase meaning temporarily, for now.

clue.text: Fool putting mother's ruin in beakers

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the drinking vessels

parts.note: beakers are drinking cups, mugs
mother's ruin is an old British slang name for gin

explanation.surface: An idiot pours gin into the cups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mother's ruin' is a British nickname for gin. Muggins is British slang for a gullible person, often oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Muggins is a British informal term for a dupe or simpleton.

clue.text: Intended securing new funds

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: one's intended is one's fiance, the person one is engaged to

explanation.surface: A fiance locking up fresh money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' is a noun meaning betrothed, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Finance means money resources, the monetary backing for a project.

clue.text: Fine man crossing street is cold

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: crossing here means stretching across, so the name goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: Roy is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man in good health walks across the road and feels chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Frosty means icy or very chilly, covered with frost.

clue.text: Small vicious old woman in exchange

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
witch is a derogatory term for a spiteful old woman

explanation.surface: A tiny nasty crone involved in a swap.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch is to swap or trade one thing for another.

clue.text: Saw nothing untoward in "new" town

indicators.note: untoward means unusual or improper, so these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone saw nothing odd in a newly built town.
explanation.walkthrough: Washington in Tyne and Wear, north-east England, was designated a British new town in 1964.
explanation.definitionFit: Washington is one of the planned towns built in post-war Britain under the New Towns Act.

clue.text: Jargon used by coarse woman around north

indicators.note: around means the first piece encircles the abbreviation

parts.note: slag is offensive British ... for a vulgar woman

explanation.surface: Rough talk from a crude woman about the north.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal vocabulary of a group, close to jargon.

clue.text: Principal male character appearing in theatre-in-the-round

indicators.note: appearing in means found inside the run of letters

explanation.surface: The leading man takes the stage in a round auditorium.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero is the lead male role in a story or drama.

clue.text: Cut legs, tripping up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: pins is informal slang for legs

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles and gashes their legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tripping up' turns PINS upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a small cut made with scissors.

clue.text: Derelict carriage housing male

indicators.note: housing means containing, so one piece shelters the other

parts.note: a trap is a light two-wheeled horse carriage

explanation.surface: A dilapidated carriage with a man living in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A derelict, as a noun, is a homeless vagrant, the same as a down-and-out wanderer.

clue.text: Under canvas next to one, on purpose

parts.note: being under canvas means living in a tent
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Camping beside someone deliberately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on purpose' reads as one phrase, but ON is a piece and 'purpose' alone is the definition; 'next to' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An intention is an aim or plan, what one means to do.

clue.text: Significant increase in salary in tower block

definitions.meaning: a big pay rise, read as a large increment
a tall building of many storeys

explanation.surface: A generous pay rise for those in the skyscraper.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is a large pay increase; as one term it is a tall building of many floors.

clue.text: A coin for each one

parts.note: a piece is a coin, as in a fifty-pence piece

explanation.surface: One coin given to every person.
explanation.definitionFit: Apiece means respectively, every one getting the stated amount.
